blocks.title: Give the agent clean Markdown from the pages it needs
blocks.description: Scrape one page, list a site's URLs, crawl a section depth-limited, read a PDF or Word file, download a video, and watch every fetch in an animated spider console. Works on its own, or through your Firecrawl API key for OCR, stealth proxying and scheduled monitors.

showcase.user_prompt: Crawl the Astravia plugin docs under /docs/plugin and tell me what I need to declare for an activity tab.
showcase.assistant_reply: Crawled 9 pages under /docs/plugin (12-page limit, depth 2, sitemap seeded). The tab contract is in ui-slots.md: a plugin registers a component with zero props, declares scope_use, and must keep its UI inside the panel rectangle — no fixed positioning or portals. Two links to the changelog were refused by the /docs/plugin scope, and one /blog link by the exclude rule.

items.title: Ten tools, one answer shape
items.description: scrape, batch_scrape, crawl, map, search, extract, parse, video, job_status and monitor. The same call works whether the local engine or your Firecrawl API answers it, so prompts and habits transfer.

items.title: Pages that need JavaScript
items.description: Static HTML first; the host browser takes over when the page is an app shell or the text is too thin. Screenshots, wait-for and click actions are supported.

items.title: Documents, not just HTML
items.description: PDFs keep their text layer and page count; DOCX and XLSX are read as documents with headings, lists and tables instead of being refused as binary.

items.title: Video and audio you can keep
items.description: HLS and DASH streams are read segment by segment and written as one file through the save dialog. Encrypted and DRM-protected streams are named as such, not worked around.

items.title: Honest about what it skipped
items.description: Every refused link carries a reason — depth, scope, pattern, robots.txt, file type, social media — and the count is reported instead of quietly dropping pages.

items.title: Spider console
items.description: The start page sits in the middle and each hop moves outward one ring. Spiders drop onto the page being fetched, packets travel down the active spokes, and refused links stay visible as dashed threads.

blocks.content:
## Two engines, one console

The console header carries an engine bar:

- **auto** — Firecrawl API when an endpoint or key is set, local engine otherwise.
- **API** — always the Firecrawl v2 API (api.firecrawl.dev or your own instance). Adds OCR for scanned PDFs, stealth proxying, a hosted job queue and cron-scheduled monitors.
- **local** — always in-plugin. No key, no account, no per-page cost.

The API key lives in the host credential vault; it is never written to a config file, never shown again after saving, and never passed as a tool argument.

## Reading the spider web

- **Center dot** — the page you started from; each ring outward is one link hop.
- **Solid dot** — page fetched and converted. **Hollow dashed dot** — link refused; hover the console for the rule.
- **Spider with a pulse ring** — being fetched right now; the moving packet is the request travelling down that spoke.
- **Red ×** — request failed (timeout, HTTP error, unsupported content type).

Animation only runs while the tab is visible and the crawl is live, and it is disabled automatically when your system asks for reduced motion.

items.title: Install and enable the plugin
items.description: The Crawler tab appears in the activity panel, and the agent gains the firecrawl tools plus the skill.

items.title: Optional: connect your Firecrawl API
items.description: Open the engine bar and paste an endpoint and key. Skip it to stay entirely local.

items.title: Paste a URL and crawl
items.description: Defaults are 12 pages and depth 2. Widen them only if you need more; the console explains every refusal.

items.title: Or just ask
items.description: “Crawl example.com/docs and summarize the API pages”, “read this PDF as Markdown”, “download the video on this page”. The agent picks the tool and the same console follows along.

blocks.content: Unencrypted HLS/DASH segments are downloaded and joined. DRM (Widevine/PlayReady/FairPlay) and encrypted playlists are reported, never decrypted. robots.txt is honoured, logins and captchas are not defeated, and requests come from your machine.
